items.title: Comparative evaluation of class activation mapping-based explainable artificial intelligence methods for target detection in optical remote sensing using YOLOv5
items.abstract: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has become a critical component in the deployment of deep learning-based object detection models, particularly in remote sensing applications where complex scenes, heterogeneous targets, and safety-critical decisions demand transparency and interpretability. Among XAI techniques, class activation mapping (CAM)-based methods are widely adopted; however, their relative effectiveness in object detection settings, particularly under varying scene complexity and target density, remains insufficiently explored. In this study, a systematic qualitative and quantitative evaluation of CAM-based XAI methods for target detection in optical remote sensing imagery is conducted, using the YOLOv5 architecture as the underlying detector. The evaluated methods are Grad-CAM, Grad-CAM++, XGrad-CAM, Eigen-CAM, Score-CAM, KPCA-CAM, Shapley-CAM, and Finer-CAM. Experiments are performed on the DIOR dataset, which provides a diverse set of object classes and scene configurations representative of real-world high-resolution remote sensing imagery. To quantitatively evaluate CAM-based explanations, a masking-based evaluation framework is employed, consisting of two primary strategies (M1 and M2), and complemented by an additional entropy-based analysis (M3). The M1 and M2 strategies evaluate the relevance and sufficiency of CAM-highlighted regions by selectively removing or preserving salient areas and analyzing the resulting changes in detection performance. In addition, an adapted M3 strategy based on Bernoulli entropy is introduced to analyze changes in the Bernoulli entropy derived from detector confidence scores under CAM-guided perturbations, providing a complementary assessment of the spatial concentration of CAM explanations around annotated targets. The experimental results reveal substantial variation in the behavior of the evaluated CAM methods, demonstrating that no single explanation approach is universally optimal across all evaluation criteria. Instead, CAM selection should consider application requirements and be supported by quantitative evaluation rather than relying solely on qualitative visualization. The proposed evaluation framework provides a systematic basis for comparing and selecting CAM-based explanation methods for remote sensing target detection.

items.title: Compartmentalized Resilience Architecture for Mission-Critical Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
items.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) increasingly integrate autonomous navigation, wireless communication, artificial intelligence, and modular payloads, increasing the risk that faults or cyberattacks may propagate to flight-critical functions. This paper proposes a compartmentalized resilience architecture for autonomous, network-connected, mission-critical UAVs. It separates flight control, navigation, communication, mission autonomy, payload processing, data management, and safety monitoring into distinct trust domains. A default-deny policy gateway governs inter-compartment communication, while an adaptive trust mechanism restricts or quarantines abnormal components and activates predefined recovery modes. The architecture is assessed through a comparative analytical framework covering representative fault and attack scenarios. The assessment considers containment, flight safety, mission continuity, response time, and anticipated resource overhead. The paper also reviews major UAV applications and their challenges and outlines how compartmentalization can support a modular UAV platform with interchangeable subsystems. The approach aims to limit fault propagation and preserve safe operation while accounting for UAV real-time and resource constraints.

items.title: Complexity-Aware Surgical Video Reasoning Segmentation with Digital Twin and Context Memory
items.abstract: Conventional surgical segmentation relies on closed-set categories or explicit text queries, which cannot resolve implicit queries that require reasoning about workflows, instrument functions, and temporal relationships. To address these limitations, we propose SurgReasonSeg, a complexity-aware method that brings reasoning segmentation over digital twin (DT) representations to surgical video. Specifically, SurgReasonSeg constructs DT representations from surgical foundation models and trains two low-rank adapters (LoRA) of one large language model with reinforcement learning (RL), each specialized for a different query complexity. A lightweight router, also trained with RL, selects between the two adapters to balance latency against accuracy. SurgReasonSeg also sets the temporal context with an adaptive sliding window conditioned on query complexity and workflow phase, and retrieves relevant historical cases from a surgical context memory by workflow similarity and procedural relevance. We further introduce EndoVis-ReasonSeg, a surgical reasoning segmentation benchmark with 1,460 training and 961 test samples across semantic, spatial, and temporal categories. On EndoVis-ReasonSeg, SurgReasonSeg improves J&F over the strongest baseline, ReSurgSAM2, by 0.178, 0.237, and 0.297 on semantic, spatial, and temporal queries, and it also achieves the best results on the Ref-EndoVis17 and Ref-EndoVis18 referring segmentation benchmarks. A backbone-matched attribution protocol separates the contribution of the upstream segmenter from that of the reasoning modules. Our method runs at 18.8 FPS averaged over the query distribution, enabling real-time reasoning segmentation in surgical videos.

items.title: Conclusion
items.abstract: This concluding chapter synthesizes the theoretical, methodological, and applied contributions of the monograph, positioning Artificial Intelligence as a transformative yet inherently constrained tool within Sports Science. It integrates insights from four core sections, spanning foundational concepts, practical AI modeling, and emerging ethical and governance challenges. The chapter highlights how Artificial Intelligence enables advanced prediction, pattern recognition, and decision support in sport, while emphasizing that its effectiveness depends on data quality, methodological rigor, and responsible interpretation. The chapter further underscores the dual nature of AI as both an analytical enhancer and a potential source of bias, overreliance, and ethical risk. Key contributions of the monograph—such as the AI-Sport Reporting Checklist (AI-SRC), the Fair Play AI (PLAY) Framework, and the Curriculum Design Framework—are presented as integrative tools that operationalize transparency, accountability, and ethical governance in both research and education. Finally, the chapter outlines future directions, including the integration of multimodal data, autonomous systems, and interdisciplinary collaboration, while stressing the growing importance of AI literacy in Sports Science. It concludes that the long-term value of Artificial Intelligence in sport depends not only on technological advancement but on its alignment with human expertise, ethical standards, and the fundamental values of sport.

items.abstract: The economics of artificial intelligence cannot be reduced to a simple story of machines replacing workers, firms becoming more efficient, or governments struggling to regulate a new technology. AI affects the economy through multiple channels at once. It lowers the cost of prediction, expands the range of automatable cognitive tasks, changes the boundaries of firms, increases the value of data and compute, alters the distribution of income, creates new risks in finance, and forces states to reconsider how they tax, spend, regulate, and provide social insurance.

items.title: Context-Aware Multimodal Efficient Navigation in VR
items.abstract: Navigation is a fundamental task in virtual reality, where efficiency is crucial. Conventional virtual reality navigation methods often require users to learn complex controls, struggle to interpret user intent, and become inefficient in complex environments. We propose VR Guider, a multimodal navigation method incorporating a large language model (LLM). Our method integrates natural language, gestures, head-motion and field-of-view (FoV) cues to enable adaptive semantic navigation. Specifically, the system constructs a structured object-level scene representation and aligns it with multimodal user inputs. The LLM reasons over this context to infer user intent and generates structured navigation commands for adaptive viewpoint control. A user study in two virtual environments showed that VR Guider significantly improved task-completion efficiency relative to representative baselines and achieved the highest usability score (SUS = 87.97). A controlled ablation study further showed that multimodal cues, interaction history, and LLM reasoning improved target selection.

items.title: Contextual Candour: Role-Aware Graduated Disclosure for LLMs over Mixed-Sensitivity Contexts
items.abstract: LLMs increasingly operate over mixed-sensitivity contexts, where they must reason over information ranging from public to confidential while disclosing only what the user is authorised to receive. Existing approaches enforce access control as a binary decision: either fully answering or refusing, without regulating how much or what kind of information is revealed if access is granted, leading to over-refusal or unintended leakage. We introduce graduated disclosure, an access-control formulation in which the level of detail and sensitivity in a model's response is calibrated to the user's authorisation rather than treated as a grant-or-deny decision. We model graduated disclosure as a disclosure-aware generation problem and propose a reward-based optimisation framework that shapes responses toward level-appropriate abstractions while penalising unauthorised factual leakage, including paraphrases and approximations. We evaluate our approach on enterprise and clinical benchmarks and compare it with prompt-based, gating, and supervised baselines. Experiments show that our method substantially reduces information leakage while preserving correctness and utility. These results suggest that disclosure control must be integrated into the generation process itself to enable secure yet useful LLM deployments.

items.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring for Metabolic Phenotyping and Precision Nutrition: Current Evidence, Clinical Applications and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has evolved beyond conventional diabetes management into an enabling technology for metabolic phenotyping and precision nutrition by providing continuous, real-world assessment of individual glycemic responses to dietary and lifestyle exposures. This narrative review examines the principles and clinical utility of CGM and its emerging applications in metabolic monitoring and personalized nutrition, with particular emphasis on postprandial glycemic variability, computational prediction, dietary feedback, and behavioral interventions. A literature search was conducted in Web of Science, PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar using predefined combinations of terms related to CGM, precision and personalized nutrition, diet, postprandial glycemic responses, lifestyle, glycemic variability, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computational nutrition, including English-language literature available up to June 2026. Current evidence demonstrates substantial interindividual variability in postprandial glycemic responses and supports the potential integration of CGM with dietary, clinical, anthropometric, behavioral, and microbiome-derived data to characterize individual metabolic responses and inform individualized prediction and nutritional guidance. However, the reproducibility and generalizability of CGM-derived metabolic phenotypes and predictive models remain incompletely established. CGM-supported nutritional and behavioral interventions have demonstrated improvements in glycemic and selected cardiometabolic outcomes, particularly in individuals with type 2 diabetes, whereas evidence of clinical benefit in populations without diabetes remains substantially more limited. Sustained engagement and psychological, technical, and accessibility-related limitations also remain important considerations. Emerging multi-analyte sensing technologies may further broaden continuous metabolic assessment and support more comprehensive, data-driven precision-nutrition strategies.

items.title: Corpus Quality Improves, Retrieval Utility Does Not: An Ablation of Preprocessing and Refinement in a Speech-to-QA Pipeline
items.abstract: Practitioners building training corpora with a pipeline of language models keep a preprocessing or refinement (post-process) stage when switching it on raises the corpus quality. We ablate a production pipeline that turns conference speech into question-answer pairs. The preprocessing stage rewrites the transcript, and the refinement stage filters the generated pairs. Switching each on and off gives four corpora from the same 40 Korean medical and finance sessions. On the corpus itself, quality rises as the stages switch on. Four LLM judges and six human domain experts rank the four corpora the same way, and the fully refined corpus leads by +0.18 and +0.22 on a 1-5 scale. We then ask whether that gain carries downstream. We supply each corpus to six models at inference and measure retrieval accuracy. The ranking does not hold. Enabling the transcript rewrite lowers retrieval accuracy by 0.061, the only stage effect that survives correction for multiple comparisons. That stage also reads the whole session, so it almost doubles the cost of one. With both stages on, accuracy does not change. An equivalence test we declared in advance confirms this. items.title: Correlations Between Test Anxiety and Self-Determination Among Introductory Biology Students
items.abstract: Self-determination theory (SDT) is a psychological framework concerning human motivation and personal growth. It holds that when the basic psychological needs of autonomy, competence, and relatedness are met, people are more likely to be driven by intrinsic rather than extrinsic motivation in achieving goals. In this study, we looked at 12 sections of an introductory majors’ biology class to see if weekly participation in a student-led classroom activity would increase measures of SDT constructs, leading to increased intrinsic motivation and decreased test anxiety. We used previously validated scales to assess test anxiety, engagement, needs satisfaction, and intrinsic vs. extrinsic motivation. Our data show a strong inverse correlation between engagement and test anxiety, and a strong negative correlation between needs satisfaction and test anxiety. This study provides further evidence supporting the idea that psychological measures associated with SDT are correlated with student test anxiety. While we did not find any association between the activity and the measures studied, the fact that Basic Needs Satisfaction scores are inversely correlated with test anxiety supports the conclusion that fulfilling students’ need for autonomy, relatedness, and competence can be associated with reduced test anxiety.

items.title: Coupled prediction of fishery output value based on coupling coordination features and machine learning
items.abstract: In response to the neglect of the complex coupling relationship between fishing and aquaculture subsystems and the difficulty of quantifying interactive effects in traditional fishery output value prediction, which leads to insufficient prediction accuracy, this study is based on time-series data from 1986 to 2023. The entropy method is used to calculate the comprehensive development index for fishing and aquaculture, and then the coupling and coordination degrees are determined. The two are used as enhanced features, along with original variables (yield, operation intensity, aquaculture area, etc.), as inputs to the random forest model. Firstly, standardize the raw data and handle missing values; Secondly, construct a random forest model with coupled features and use Bayesian optimization for hyperparameter tuning; Simultaneously, set up a benchmark model without feature coupling for comparison. The results show that the optimized coupled enhanced random forest model has a coefficient of determination R^2=0.923 and a root mean square error of 692 million yuan, which is better than the benchmark model with R^2=0.891 and RMSE=874 million yuan. From 1986 to 2023, the coordination degree increased from 0.262 to 0.540, and the subsystems developed from severe imbalance to primary coordination. The feature importance analysis based on a random forest shows that the combined weight of the coupling degree and the coordination degree is significantly higher than that of any single yield indicator and is a key driver of fluctuations in the output value. The use of artificial intelligence methods to quantify subsystem interactions provides data support for short-term fishery management decisions and medium- to long-term industrial planning and enhances prediction reliability by identifying coupling features.

items.title: Credit Card Fraud Detection Using Machine Learning
items.abstract: Credit card fraud is a significant challenge in digital financial transactions, causing financial losses to customers, banks, and financial institutions. Traditional fraud detection systems rely on predefined rules and manual verification, which may fail to identify complex and continuously changing fraudulent patterns. This project proposes an artificial-intelligence-based credit card fraud detection system using machine learning to classify financial transactions as legitimate or potentially fraudulent. The system uses the publicly available European credit card fraud detection dataset from Kaggle. Data preprocessing, feature scaling, and class-imbalance handling with class weighting are applied. SMOTE is not used. Logistic Regression is the baseline classifier, and Random Forest is the primary classifier. The system integrates a Python backend with a MySQL database and a web interface. The application is an academic demonstration and does not connect to a live banking or payment network.

items.title: Critical Data Literacies for Young People in the Age of Online Advertising
items.abstract: Abstract This chapter examines critical data literacies and the implications of the data-driven, targeted, online advertising systems that increasingly shape young people’s health and well-being. It argues that targeted online advertising is not merely a marketing technique but part of a broader sociotechnical infrastructure built on surveillance, behavioural profiling, data extraction, and algorithmic optimisation. These systems mean young people are constantly exposed to advertisements representing risk factors for adverse health outcomes, including unhealthy food and beverages, alcohol, gambling, vaping products, and tobacco. These very systems also curate young people’s digital experience by influencing what they see, who they follow, and what captures their attention. In doing so, they shape consumption patterns, social norms, and emotional well-being, while disproportionately burdening those already vulnerable to harm. In this context, critical data literacies are understood as the interpretive, political, and civic capacities required to understand how data are collected, analysed, monetised, and mobilised to shape behaviour, opportunities, risks, and well-being. The chapter argues that such literacies are essential to support youth agency, collective voice, and informed participation in digital environments by enabling young people to critically interrogate the commercial logics, power relations, and hidden infrastructures underpinning online advertising systems and imagine alternative futures. The chapter also argues that critical data literacies alone are insufficient to address the harms caused by the current online advertising system. Meaningful reform also requires structural and regulatory interventions that address the underlying political and economic conditions of data-driven advertising systems.

items.title: Critical Fairness Literacy for PK–12 teachers: a fairness-specific dimension of teacher AI competency
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes integrated into PK–12 education, teachers need professional judgment to evaluate its fairness. This conceptual paper develops Critical Fairness Literacy (CFL) through a structured synthesis of literature on teacher AI competency, critical AI literacy, algorithmic fairness, educational AI ethics, and educational equity. CFL is proposed as a subdimension of teacher AI competency focused on fairness, comprising bias source identification, contextual equity analysis, and interrogation of fairness definitions. Three practical protocols, bias tracing, equity-centered contextual review, and fairness framing reflection, connect these dimensions to classroom judgment and professional learning. The paper proposes how guided inquiry, peer feedback, and repeated application might support CFL development. The framework and protocols remain theoretically informed proposals requiring empirical investigation.

items.title: CRITICISM OF POSTHUMANISM, TRANSHUMANISM, AND JUSTIFICATION FOR RECOGNIZING TECHNOLOGICALLY MODIFIED HUMANS
items.abstract: The article analyzes posthumanism and transhumanism as competing philosophical discourses that construct the techno-modified subject in different ways within contemporary technoculture. The accelerated development of NBIC technologies, artificial intelligence systems, and bioengineering shifts the technological modification of human beings into the realm of acute socio-political problems. Practices of genetic editing and cyborgization highlight issues concerning the boundaries of the human, the redistribution of resources, and new configurations of power and inequality. The author shows that the posthumanist perspective provides a critical vocabulary for deconstructing the boundaries between the human and the non-human, as well as for detailing distributed and hybrid subjectivity. However, the radical deconstruction of the autonomous subject complicates the development of positive normative criteria: it becomes unclear how to allocate responsibility, justice, and dignity within complex networks of relations. Transhumanism, in turn, articulates the values of autonomy and the right to technological self-improvement aimed at overcoming biological limitations, enhancing cognitive abilities, and radically extending lifespan. Nevertheless, this project does not sufficiently take into account the socio-political consequences of techno-differences. The dominant techno-commercial versions of transhumanism have an individualistic orientation and ignore risks such as unequal access to technologies, the exclusion of “unenhanced” individuals, and status conflicts. As an alternative framework, the article draws on the tradition of Russian cosmism, where overcoming human limitations is conceived not as an individual privilege, but as a collective “common cause” based on solidarity and equal access. The author concludes that it is necessary to supplement these discourses with theories of recognition and the analysis of practices of inclusion and exclusion. The integration of the category of recognition will allow moving from the critique of future scenarios to the development of a comprehensive normative model of technoculture, where overcoming limitations is combined with preserving the dignity and mutual respect of the participants in social interaction.

items.title: Cross-Platform AI Modeling in Sports Science
items.abstract: This chapter presents a practical application of Artificial Intelligence through neural network regression in the context of professional tennis performance analysis. The objective is to model and predict total prize money based on relative performance indicators and contextual variables, thereby illustrating how AI can support data-driven decision-making in competitive sport environments. The chapter emphasizes the importance of using normalized and relative metrics rather than absolute values to ensure comparability across players with varying participation levels. The modeling workflow is developed within a structured analytical framework, including data preprocessing, feature construction, model training, and evaluation. Particular attention is given to the interpretation of model outputs and the limitations associated with neural network approaches, including potential overfitting and reduced interpretability. The chapter also demonstrates how AI models can integrate both performance and non-performance variables to provide a more holistic understanding of athlete success. Through this case study, the chapter highlights the practical relevance of neural networks in sports analytics, offering insights into performance modeling, financial outcomes, and strategic planning. It serves as a foundational example of how machine learning techniques can be operationalized in real-world sport contexts while maintaining methodological transparency and analytical rigor.

items.title: Cross-Platform Bayesian Approach
items.abstract: This chapter presents an advanced application of Artificial Intelligence through Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) in the context of sports performance modeling. Building on previous regression and classification approaches, the chapter introduces a probabilistic deep learning framework that explicitly incorporates uncertainty into model predictions. The objective is to estimate performance-related outcomes while quantifying both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty, thereby providing more robust and informative predictions for decision-making in sport contexts. The chapter outlines a complete modeling pipeline, including data preprocessing, feature engineering, network architecture design, model training, and posterior inference. Particular emphasis is placed on uncertainty estimation, posterior sampling, and the interpretation of predictive distributions rather than single-point estimates. The advantages of Bayesian approaches over deterministic neural networks are critically discussed, especially in relation to limited data, variability, and the need for transparent inference. Through an applied case study, the chapter demonstrates how Bayesian Neural Networks can support performance prediction, risk assessment, and strategic planning in sports analytics. It positions BNNs as a state-of-the-art modeling approach within Sports Science, contributing to the integration of deep learning, Bayesian inference, and explainable artificial intelligence in applied research and practice.

items.title: CT Ventricular Volume Reference Percentile Curves Using Automated nnU-Net Segmentation: A Study with LLM-Facilitated Cohort Selection
items.abstract: Background: Age- and sex-specific CT reference percentile curves of ventricular volume may support objective assessment of ventricular enlargement. We aimed to generate such curves by combining a locally deployed large language model (LLM) for cohort curation with nnU-Net 12-subcompartment segmentation. Methods: This retrospective study did not require formal ethics approval under the Swiss Human Research Act. We screened 42,211 head CT reports from January 2019 to April 2024. A phrase prefilter identified 9622 candidates for German-tuned 70-billion-parameter LLM review of stroke, leukoencephalopathy, parenchymal defects, enlarged ventricles, and space-occupying lesions; 6516 remained. A second LLM workflow screened 210,761 clinical data warehouse summaries to exclude dementia, organic brain disease, or cognitive decline. After image-availability and series-mismatch exclusions, the final cohort comprised 2608 CTs from 2608 patients (1374 males, 1234 females; age 14–98 years). Ventricular masks were obtained using a validated nnU-Net tool integrated in TotalSegmentator. Results: LLM labelling accuracy in 471 blinded reports ranged from 0.966 to 0.992. CDW screening audit showed 91% agreement, sensitivity 0.96, and negative predictive value 0.96. Median total ventricular volume rose from 10.94 mL in young females and 13.42 mL in young males to 21.97 mL and 31.97 mL, respectively, in the 60–69 age group. Except for the fourth ventricle, compartments showed positive age correlations (r = 0.44–0.69); the fourth ventricle showed no relevant association (r = 0.01 males; r = 0.05 females). After adjustment for age, male sex remained associated with greater total ventricular volume (6.54 mL; 95% CI, 5.61–7.46; p<0.001). Conclusions: This study provides age- and sex-specific CT ventricular nomograms in a selected reference cohort. The LLM-assisted curation and nnU-Net segmentation workflow provides a feasible approach for large-scale cohort analysis.

items.title: Data Engineering and Large Language Model Construction for the Food Safety Domain
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in natural language processing; however, their direct application to food safety remains limited by insufficient domain knowledge, inadequate reasoning over regulatory documents, and the tendency to generate factual hallucinations. To address these challenges, this study proposes FSLLM, a domain-specific LLM designed for food safety applications. A high-quality domain corpus was constructed from diverse sources, including food safety incidents, regulatory documents, inspection reports, and industry-related materials. It initially comprised approximately 150 million tokens, of which 45,024 documents and approximately 121 million tokens were retained after decontamination. Based on the Qwen3-8B foundation model, FSLLM was developed through a two-stage training framework consisting of continual pre-training for domain knowledge adaptation and supervised fine-tuning for task alignment. Furthermore, a comprehensive benchmark covering 10 representative food safety tasks, including named entity recognition, text classification, text generation, factual verification, regulatory compliance analysis, and public health question answering, was established for systematic evaluation. Experimental results show that FSLLM outperforms the base model across multiple food safety tasks. Specifically, FSLLM achieved a Micro-F1 score of 0.5286 in named entity recognition and an accuracy of 85.21% in food safety event classification, demonstrating improvements over the base model. These findings indicate that domain-specific corpus and continual pre-training with fine-tuning enhance LLM expertise and reasoning, offering a viable solution for intelligent food safety supervision and risk analysis.

items.title: Data Quality Challenges in Artificial Intelligence: Impacts of Missing, Mislabeled and Biased Data on Machine Learning
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is developing at a high speed and is now used in many places. AI models need a large amount of data to some extent; therefore, problems in the data can lead to errors in the model. The three main types of harmful data that are the subject of this study are biased, mislabelled and missing data. If a large part of the data set is missing, it will result in information loss and a lower-performing model. In addition, the model may be incorrectly trained due to mislabelled data and thus unreliable. If the data are biased, then there will be discrimination against some groups. Some possible countermeasures have also been mentioned in the discussion. Imputation or Deletion Methods are used to address missing values. Data cleaning, label verification and noise-robust learning can all reduce mislabelled data. Bias in the data can be addressed before, during and after model training. Generally speaking, there is no single way to handle all the data problems. Different datasets and problems have different solutions, so they will be different.

items.title: Data-Centric Recursive Improvement for Foundation Models: A Survey
items.abstract: Data-centric methods are central to foundation model development, but data construction and evaluation have often been treated as separate stages. Recent model-development pipelines increasingly couple the two: evaluation results expose capability gaps and failure modes, which then guide data selection, filtering, synthesis, and post-training interventions that shape the behavior of subsequent model versions. This survey studies this trend as data-centric recursive improvement, with data-evaluation co-evolution as its core mechanism. In this mechanism, evaluation produces diagnostic signals, orchestration determines whether and how these signals should be trusted and used, and execution updates mutable data-related objects. These updated objects are then used in later training, adaptation, retrieval, or memory stages, enabling the system to change in subsequent rounds. The framework centers on three questions: what signal diagnoses the current system, who decides how to act on that signal, and what object is updated to affect the next round. We organize the literature around this signal-decision-update loop, covering feedback signals, control decisions, and data updates across major stages of foundation model development. We further examine failure modes in closed-loop improvement, such as unreliable feedback, feedback overfitting, unstable updates, erosion of data support, and irreproducible system changes. By providing a structured framework for understanding and designing data-evaluation co-evolution, this survey outlines a roadmap toward more adaptive, robust, and accountable foundation model development, where evaluation becomes an active driver of recursive model improvement rather than a passive measure of progress and ultimately sheds light on possible pathways toward Artificial Super Intelligence (ASI), in which a model continually evolve and surpass human-level performance across diverse tasks. All surveyed papers are organized in a public repository https://github.com/zoezou2015/Awesome-Data-Centric-Recursive-Improvement.

items.title: Data-Driven Optimisation of Superconducting Magnets at CEA Paris-Saclay
items.abstract: Superconducting magnets for particle accelerators are particularly challenging to design because they involve a large number of coupled physical phenomena and the management of complex datasets. Artificial Intelligence, including machine learning and advanced optimisation techniques, offers promising approaches to address these challenges and accelerate the design process. This paper presents a new advanced optimisation and data management platform, together with its underlying software infrastructure and integration into design simulations. It also highlights several ongoing applications of advanced optimisation methods carried out at CEA Paris-Saclay, including multiphysics optimisation using active learning, topology optimisation, holistic modelling of an Electron Cyclotron Resonance (ERC) ion source, and anomaly detection in quench events.

items.title: Decolonising Generative Artificial Intelligence in African Higher Education: Toward Ubuntu-ẸkỌ, Augmented Collective Wisdom and Digital Sovereignty
items.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into higher education presents both significant opportunities and critical challenges for institutions in Africa and the wider Global South. While GenAI can expand access to information, support teaching and learning, and strengthen research productivity, its deployment also raises questions concerning whose knowledge is represented, which languages are privileged, how credibility is constructed, and who exercises control over the infrastructures and data on which artificial intelligence depends. This article critically examined the implications of these challenges through the lenses of decolonial theory, epistemic justice, African philosophical thought, and critical AI studies. Rather than treating artificial intelligence as a culturally neutral technological artefact, the article conceptualises AI as a sociotechnical system whose knowledge practices are shaped by historical, economic, linguistic and epistemological relations of power. Drawing on a critical interpretive synthesis of scholarly literature, policy documents and African philosophical perspectives, the article developed the Ubuntu-Ẹ̀kọ́ Framework as an original conceptual contribution. The framework brings together relationality, ethical character, contextual responsiveness, critical consciousness and communal capability. Building on this framework, the article proposes Augmented Collective Wisdom (ACW) as a reorientation of AI from a technology primarily designed to automate or individualise knowledge work toward a sociotechnical resource that supports collective learning, human judgement, cultural integrity and community wellbeing. The article further advanced Digital Sovereignty as a strategic alternative to a narrow discourse of AI readiness. It concluded that decolonising AI in higher education does not require rejection of technological innovation; rather, it requires institutions to develop the epistemic, cultural, linguistic, infrastructural and governance capacities necessary to determine how AI is designed, interpreted, deployed and evaluated within their own contexts.

items.title: Deep Learning-Based 3D CT Body Composition Is Associated With Mortality in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Recent advances in artificial intelligence enable fully automated 3-dimensional computed tomography (CT)-based body composition quantification. We investigated whether automated CT-derived thoraco-abdominopelvic body composition measures are associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with preprocedural CT imaging were included between 2014 and 2023. A deep learning-based pipeline performed automated 3-dimensional segmentation of thoraco-abdominopelvic noncontrast CT scans to quantify volumes (L/m 2 ) and attenuations (Hounsfield units) of subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, muscular adipose tissue, and lean skeletal muscle, indexed to body surface area. Associations with mortality were evaluated using Cox models and Harrell C statistics, adjusting for demographics (age, sex, body mass index) and cardiometabolic risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, chronic renal failure). RESULTS: Among 915 patients (median age, 84 years [interquartile range, 77–90]; 58% men), 160 (17.5%) died over a median follow-up of 22 months (interquartile range, 14–36). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated that lower subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation were associated with increased mortality, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation were associated with improved survival. Addition of body composition measures provided incremental discriminatory value beyond demographics and cardiometabolic risk factors (Harrell C, 0.66 versus 0.71; P <0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Automated 3-dimensional CT-derived body composition measures provide independent prognostic information and improve risk stratification for mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Low subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation identify patients at increased risk, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation are associated with lower mortality.

items.title: Deep Learning-Based Drowsiness Prediction System using Convolutional Neural Networks
items.abstract: The high frequency of accidents caused by drowsiness underscores the critical importance of implementing efficient systems for predicting drowsiness to protect people and avert possible catastrophe. This article presents a new method for forecasting drowsiness by utilizing advanced deep learning methods, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). By utilizing improvements in computer vision and artificial intelligence, our planned system seeks to predict drowsiness accurately through the analysis of facial cues and expressions that signal fatigue. By combining a unique dataset containing a variety of facial pictures showing different levels of alertness and sleepiness, we create a strong training structure. The dataset includes samples of both closed and open eyes, yawning, and alertness, offering a detailed depiction of visual signs related to drowsiness. We use TensorFlow and Keras libraries to create and train a custom CNN model for predicting drowsiness. The suggested CNN design includes convolutional layers for extracting features, max-pooling layers for reducing dimensionality, and fully connected layers for classification. Methods like randomly flipping and rotating data are used to improve the model's ability to generalize and reduce overfitting. Moreover, incorporating batch normalization and dropout layers improves the robustness and stability of the model, making it more resistant to noise and data variability. We train the model on a carefully selected dataset and assess its performance using conventional measures including accuracy and loss. The model showed encouraging outcomes, reaching a validation accuracy of around 97.12% at the end of 41 epochs. By conducting thorough tests and confirming it, we establish the effectiveness and dependability of our suggested method in effectively identifying tiredness incidents. Our results highlight the capability of deep learning techniques in reducing the dangers linked to drowsiness-caused incidents. Our suggested system utilizes CNNs and takes advantage of facial expression analysis to provide an active method for predicting drowsiness in real-time. The consequences of this study apply to different areas like transportation safety, workplace productivity, and healthcare, involving drowsiness.

items.title: Detecting Errors in Large Language Model Responses: The Incremental Predictive Value of Hidden States
items.abstract: Although large language models support a wide range of tasks, hallucinations remain a major obstacle to user trust. When a model generates an answer, both its internal processing and final output vary with the question. Internal states are often expected to offer richer signals for hallucination detection. However, studies using these states typically report their standalone discrimination performance, while output-side comparisons often use simple baselines with weaker modeling capacity. We integrate output-side information available at inference time into a combined baseline and compare detection performance before and after adding hidden states under identical data splits and evaluation rules. Experiments cover open-ended generation and constrained multiple-choice tasks across different models. Adding hidden states improves AUROC by approximately 0.004 and 0.039 on the two tasks, respectively. Hidden states thus provide additional predictive information, but strong standalone detection performance can still yield only limited additional gains.

items.title: Developing an AI Enabled Salutogenic Leadership Model for Abadan Oil Refinery
items.abstract: To develop a context-sensitive model of artificial intelligence (AI) enabled salutogenic leadership for Abadan Oil Refinery, integrating occupational well-being with the organizational requirements of digital transformation. This applied qualitative study integrated theoretical evidence with semi-structured interviews with 18 academic and organizational experts selected purposively for their knowledge of leadership, management, and AI applications. Audio-recorded interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed in ATLAS.ti using open, axial, and selective coding. Two independent coders reconciled disagreements through discussion; the reported Cohen’s kappa was 0.79. Preliminary categories were also reviewed by participating experts. The analysis generated 140 initial open codes and a six-category paradigm model. The model comprised causal conditions, intervening conditions, contextual conditions, strategies, a core phenomenon, and anticipated outcomes. Its core combined health-promoting and sustainable leadership, psychological coherence and occupational health, and readiness for human–AI collaboration. Causal conditions concerned leadership relationships, organizational and technological drivers, and attitudes toward technology. Contextual and intervening conditions encompassed health culture, job demands and resources, digital infrastructure, psychological capacities, and digital leadership. Strategies emphasized health support, stress management, leadership development, employee learning, and responsible technological adaptation. Anticipated outcomes concerned employee health and well-being, work attitudes and engagement, and sustainable organizational performance. The model frames AI as a resource for human decision-making within a health-promoting leadership approach. It provides an exploratory framework for refinery management rather than evidence that AI implementation improves health, safety, or productivity. The proposed relationships require prospective evaluation.

items.title: Development and Innovative Applications of Tools for Monitoring Neuronal Electrical Activity
items.abstract: Neuronal electrical activity provides the most direct dynamic readout of excitability, synaptic transmission, circuit coordination, and information processing in the nervous system. Monitoring tools have evolved from intracellular and patch-clamp recordings that resolve ion-channel and membrane currents to high-density extracellular arrays, flexible neural interfaces, optical activity indicators, wireless implants, and artificial intelligence-assisted decoding systems. Each modality captures a different level of neural organization. Patch-clamp recording provides high biophysical precision at the single-cell scale, microelectrode arrays and silicon probes enable population recordings across networks, electroencephalography and functional magnetic resonance imaging support noninvasive human studies, and optical sensors map calcium, voltage, or neurochemical dynamics with cellular or subcellular resolution. Recent advances in ultraflexible electrodes, mesh electronics, genetically encoded indicators, nanomaterials, closed-loop bioelectronics, and machine learning have shifted neural monitoring from episodic measurement toward chronic, multimodal, and intervention-linked systems. This review summarizes traditional and emerging tools for monitoring neuronal electrical activity, analyzes multimodal integration strategies, and discusses applications in disease mechanism research, brain-computer interfaces, neuromodulation, brain-inspired intelligence, and neural engineering. Translation will depend on long-term biocompatibility, stable signal quality, interpretable computational models, and standards that connect device performance with biological validity.

items.title: Development and Integration of a ROSGPT-based Semantic Navigation System with Multi-user Concurrent Tasking under ROS 2
items.abstract: This paper presents a ROSGPT-based semantic navigation system for multi-user autonomous mobile robot (AMR) operation under ROS 2. An environment-specific prompt converts Traditional Chinese, English, and mixed-language requests into structured MOVE, ROTATE, and GOTO commands. JSON-format constraints, station-name whitelisting, and physical-parameter bounds are applied before command dispatch. A middleware mechanism comprising a first-in, first-out (FIFO) Task Queue, a Worker Thread, and a Dispatcher decouples request admission from cloud-based LLM inference and maintains enqueue-order task processing. Validated GOTO commands are dispatched to the Nav2 Action Server, whereas MOVE and ROTATE commands are executed by an odometry-feedback closed-loop controller. The system was evaluated through three experiments covering semantic parsing, concurrent middleware processing, and continuous physical navigation. For a predefined dataset of 150 commands, the Improved Prompt increased the Exact Match Rate from 7.3% to 100%. In a five-client workload comprising 60 requests, all requests completed semantic parsing and structured-command dispatch without observed middleware-level loss. In addition, 39 of 40 continuous physical navigation tasks were completed successfully, corresponding to a task completion rate of 97.5%. These results provide preliminary evidence of the feasibility of the proposed architecture for multi-user semantic navigation in indoor environments.

items.title: Diagnostic Performance of Deep Learning for Automated Detection of Traumatic Intracranial Hemorrhage on Non-Contrast Head Computed Tomography: A Systematic Review and Quantitative Analysis
items.abstract: This project aims to evaluate the diagnostic performance, accuracy, and workflow impact of artificial intelligence algorithms (deep learning / convolutional neural networks – CNNs) for the automated detection and characterization of traumatic intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) and indicators of severity on non-contrast head computed tomography (CT) scans in patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI). The literature search encompasses PubMed Central®, Embase®, Scopus®, Web of Science®, and Google Scholar® databases from inception through May 2026, with no language restrictions. Study selection and title and abstract screening are performed using the Rayyan CQRI tool by three reviewers in blinded mode, while full-text assessment and the final inclusion decision are conducted by a coordinator with expertise in systematic reviews, radiology, and computed tomography. Data extraction includes characteristics of the AI models (e.g., Dense-UNet, BLAST-CT, Viz.ai, AIDOC, Qure25k), diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, AUC/AUROC), hemorrhage locations readily identified by the algorithms, sources of error (false positives and false negatives), and impact on clinical management. Risk of bias is assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklist for prevalence studies, and the quality of evidence is evaluated using the GRADE system.

items.title: Die Entwicklung des Nichtraucherschutzgesetzes in Bayern: Vorbild für ganz Deutschland?
items.abstract: Background: Bavaria is a special case in Germany when it comes to tobacco control policy. The Free State initially enacted a particularly strict law protecting nonsmokers in 2008, relaxed it again in 2009, and reinstated the strict protections following the July 4, 2010 referendum. Research question: Can the Bavarian approach serve as a model for all of Germany, and what opportunities and obstacles arise when applying it to other federal states? Methods: A narrative review based on a targeted literature search, official documents, and two appended texts on developments in Bavaria. The review included political, legal, occupational health, and epidemiological studies related to the protection of nonsmokers in Bavaria and Germany. Results: The body of research consistently indicated that strict smoking bans significantly reduced exposure to secondhand smoke in indoor settings. In German restaurants and bars, fine particulate matter levels dropped dramatically after the smoking ban was introduced, and children's exposure to secondhand smoke at home and in cars decreased without any significant shift to private settings being confirmed. At the same time, the political literature showed that Bavaria's success was achieved only under specific conditions: a simple message, a clear health-based framework, strong mobilization of civil society, and a referendum question that did not hide behind exceptions. Conclusion: Bavaria serves as a model, provided this is understood as an empirically sound and politically mobilizable reference case. The model is of limited use as a blueprint because the federal legal landscape remains heterogeneous and exceptions weaken its effectiveness. The most important lesson is therefore this: protection for nonsmokers is most sustainable where it is simple, has few exceptions, and is justified as a means of protecting the workplace, children, and public health.

items.title: Disclosure Begets Disclosure: A Self-Reinforcing Privacy Loop in LLM Agents with Persistent Memory
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use persistent memory to personalize responses, and personal attributes in this memory pose a privacy risk if exposed. We ask how consulting memory during dialogue changes what users go on to say, and thus what the memory comes to reveal. In multi-session simulations, a simulated user with 24 personal attributes talks with a support agent that does or does not consult memory, and in both settings attributes are inferred from the full accumulated record. Across four support models, memory raises response quality but also empirical leakage, the share of attribute values correctly inferred from the record, by a margin that widens over sessions. The cause is a loop in ordinary, non-adversarial assistance. Memory-conditioned responses carry earlier values forward, often as presuppositions, and users affirm them or leave them uncorrected, so that cues and the agent's own guesses become recorded values. The loop reinforces itself, and removing the agent's mentions of an attribute lowers its later disclosure about twice as much as single-turn effects predict. Users cannot leave it on their own, since correcting a value discloses the attribute, declining to discuss it shifts later predictions toward sensitive values, and incorrect values left in place become entrenched. The loop is best weakened at the agent's response. Instructing the agent not to state or presuppose attributes brings leakage to about the no-memory level while keeping most of the quality gains, whereas filtering or anonymizing what users say or what is stored gives up much of them.

items.title: DIVE: Benchmarking Full-Duplex Interaction with Visual Engagement in Continuous Streams
items.abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have substantially improved spoken interaction and video understanding. Existing online and streaming benchmarks primarily assess causal multimodal perception through timestamped question answering, whereas real-world interaction requires models to continuously identify task-relevant multimodal cues and decide whether, when, and how to respond. This leaves open how well current models can sustain real-time interaction throughout an evolving multimodal stream. To address this gap, we introduce DIVE, a benchmark for evaluating full-duplex interaction with visual engagement under continuous and realistic multimodal streams. It organizes six tasks into three complementary interaction scenarios. (1) Proactive Intervention evaluates whether models can identify emerging visual or semantic cues and intervene at the appropriate moment. (2) Continuous Engagement evaluates sustained participation through continuous visual tracking and visually grounded query interaction. (3) Interaction Coordination evaluates how models coordinate listening and speaking under overlapping and multi-party interactions. DIVE contains 525 audio/video samples with fine-grained human annotations and precise temporal metadata. Its evaluation protocol separates response quality, participation decisions, and response timing. We evaluate representative real-time models using response quality, window response rates, and reaction latency. Experiments show that leading real-time models achieve sub-second average response latency, yet their average window response rates remain at or below 53.77%. Response quality varies substantially across models and tasks, with adapting ongoing responses to newly arriving information remaining particularly challenging. We hope DIVE facilitates progress toward more natural and capable real-time multimodal interactive systems.

items.title: Dopamine dynamics promote cooperative behavior not just the rewards accompanying cooperation
items.abstract: Research Hypothesis 1.Nucleus accumbens medial shell (NAcMedSh) dopamine (DA) specifically encodes 1s-synchronized successful cooperative actions, not social contact, motor execution, reward expectation or sensory cues. 2.Learned cooperation-related DA representations have asymmetric stability: they persist after switching to individual tasks, while naive animals need de novo learning for cooperation tasks. 3.NAc D1 receptor (D1R)-mediated phasic DA is necessary for cooperative behavior, with task-specific effects: low-dose D1R blockade selectively impairs cooperation without affecting basal locomotion or individual reward-seeking. Data Acquisition Data from 2-month-old male C57BL/6J mice, approved by UESTC Animal Ethics Committee. Behavioral paradigm: 1s time-window cooperative nose-poke task; paired mice get shared water reward only if nose-pokes fall within 1s, with full control paradigms. Neural recording: AAV2-hSyn-GRABDA3m injected into NAcMedSh; fiber photometry recorded DA dynamics, 405nm reference for artifact correction. Pharmacology: Bilateral NAcMedSh cannulas for microinjection of D1R antagonist SCH23390 or saline. Behavioral data: EthoVision XT 15 recorded core behavioral metrics. Dataset Structure 6 experimental folders with raw/preprocessed fiber data and behavioral markers; 4 Prism project files for statistical analysis, inter-group comparison and dose-response analysis. Key Findings & Interpretation 1.NAc DA specifically encodes cooperative actions, not external rewards: DA AUC for successful cooperation rose significantly with training (p=0.0001), failed triggers evoked no response; reward-related DA remained stable. Reward extinction eliminated reward DA, but cooperation DA stayed stable.Interpretation: Revises classic RPE theory; NAc DA assigns intrinsic motivational value to cooperation itself. 2.Asymmetric stability of cooperation DA: Cooperation-to-independent group had stable trigger DA post-switch; independent-to-cooperation group showed full de novo DA learning.Interpretation: Learned cooperation DA is consolidated like skill memory, with behavioral inertia. 3.D1R is necessary for cooperation with task specificity: Low-dose SCH23390 reduced cooperation success by 65.9% reversibly, no effect on locomotion/individual reward-seeking.Interpretation: Cooperation has higher dependence on D1R-mediated phasic DA, providing a preclinical target for social cooperation deficits. items.title: Dynamic Risk Prediction of Patient Clinical Deterioration Using Time-Aware Explainable Machine Learning
items.abstract: The early identification of clinical instability is important in intensive care because such clinical instability usually occurs along a trajectory of abnormalities but not just one abnormal value. The authors designed a time-aware explainable machine learning system that calculates every four hours the deterioration risk based on the previous 24 hours' electronic health records and predicts a new invasive mechanical ventilation, administration of vasopressors, or death in 12 hours. Time-varying vital signs, lab results, treatments, frequency, and missingness are converted into level, variability, trend, change, and recency features and analyzed using LightGBM. The treeSHAP algorithm connects subsequent predictions with changes in the patient's risk factors. The internal performance was AUROC 0.901 ± 0.005 and AUPRC 0.428 ± 0.013 in contrast to latest-value LightGBM AUROC 0.867 ± 0.006 and AUPRC 0.356 ± 0.012. In external validation, the authors obtained AUROC 0.872 ± 0.006, Brier Score 0.078 ± 0.003, and warning lead time 7.6 ± 2.9 h. Dynamic SHAP analysis revealed a pattern that the increased respiratory rate, decreasing mean arterial pressure, elevated lactate, and neurological impairment are common before a prolonged increase in risk.

items.title: Eco-Environmental, Health and Socio-Economic Perspectives on Cyanobacteria and Cyanotoxins
items.abstract: Cyanobacteria, or blue-green algae, the first oxygenic photosynthetic organisms on Earth, play indispensable ecological roles as primary producers and drivers of biogeochemical cycles, and are also sources of human food, nutraceuticals, and biotechnological products. However, cyanobacterial harmful algal blooms (CyanoHABs), intensified by eutrophication and global climate change, threaten water quality, biodiversity, and human health due to their production of diverse secondary metabolites, i.e., taste and odor (T&O) compounds and cyanotoxins. This Special Issue, “Ecology and Toxicology of Cyanobacteria and Cyanotoxins”, compiles 13 papers from 9 countries that collectively advance our understanding of these issues across multiple scales. Cyanotoxins, including microcystins, cylindrospermopsins, anatoxins, and saxitoxins, can cause various hazards to animals and humans, including systemic toxicity, hepatotoxicity, genotoxicity, carcinogenicity, reproductive/developmental toxicity, neurotoxicity, immunotoxicity, and endocrine disruption. CyanoHABs are governed by complex bottom-up and top-down regulation, and blooms and cyanotoxin production are closely linked, but not always consistent/synonymous. Environmental stressors, e.g., phosphorus limitation, cold shock, and grazing pressure, selectively favor toxigenic genotypes, or can increase the cellular cyanotoxin quota, although overall population growth is suppressed. This can be explained by the fact that cyanotoxins can help cyanobacteria to better adapt to environmental stressors. When blooms disperse, demise, or are disrupted by certain interventions, the reduced biomass may increase exposure to dissolved, extra-cellular cyanotoxins if intra-cellular toxins are released faster than they are degraded or removed. We term the uncoupling of biomass and toxicity as the “cyanobacterial biomass–toxicity paradox”. We propose a “3P framework”, i.e., prediction, prevention, and prioritization, for the evidence-based risk management of CyanoHABs and cyanotoxins. We also advocate for more studies using multi-omics and artificial intelligence, as well as multi-disciplinary, multi-sectoral, and multi-stakeholder collaboration under the “One Health” umbrella to translate science into actionable solutions for sustainable development.

items.title: Edukasi ergonomi dan pendampingan penerapan pestisida nabati daun mimba pada kelompok tani di Kota Metro
items.abstract: Background: Agricultural activities involve physical demands and the use of pesticides, which can potentially lead to occupational health issues for farmers. Problems may arise from the use of chemical pesticides, which can cause poisoning, skin irritation, nausea, nervous system disorders, hypertension, anemia, and even cognitive impairments. Purpose: To provide education on agricultural ergonomics and to assist a farmer group in learning about and applying botanical pesticides specifically those derived from neem leaves on rice crops. Method: The activity was conducted on July 29–30, 2026, in RW 03, Margodadi Village, Metro Selatan District, Metro City, Lampung, involving 23 members of a farmer group. The stages of the activity included identifying issues through observation and discussion, presenting material via PowerPoint, facilitating discussions and Q&A sessions, demonstrating the preparation of neem leaf extract (led by students), and providing guidance on the application of the extract to crops. Evaluation was carried out descriptively by observing participant engagement, discussions, Q&A sessions, and the application of spraying techniques for the botanical pesticide, with a focus on reducing ergonomic risks and assessing the effectiveness of the pesticide used. Results: All participants (23 individuals; 100%) attended the educational sessions and field-based guidance. Participants were actively involved in discussions, demonstrations, and the practical application of spraying equipment and botanical pesticides in the fields. The activity provided the participants with an introduction to and practical experience regarding ergonomic principles and the use of neem leaves as an alternative pest control method. Conclusion: Education on ergonomics and guidance on the application of neem-leaf-based botanical pesticides were successfully implemented, effectively enhancing the community's understanding of the health risks associated with pesticides. The demonstration of botanical pesticide preparation, combined with hands-on guidance, provided direct experience in simple ergonomic practices for using spray equipment and highlighted the benefits of using botanical alternatives to conventional pesticides. Suggestion: Future activities should incorporate more measurable evaluation designs, ergonomic risk assessment instruments, documentation of musculoskeletal complaints, and quantitative observation of pest populations and crop damage. Keywords: Agricultural ergonomics education; Botanical pesticides; Farmers; Neem leaves; Occupational health Pendahuluan: Kegiatan pertanian melibatkan tuntutan fisik dan penggunaan pestisida yang berpotensi menimbulkan masalah kesehatan kerja pada petani. Permasalahan yang terjadi dapat disebabkan dari penggunaan pestisida kimia yang dapat menyebabkan keracunan, iritasi kulit, mual, gangguan sistem saraf, hipertensi, anemia, hingga masalah kognitif. Tujuan: Untuk memberikan edukasi mengenai ergonomi pertanian serta mendampingi kelompok tani dalam mengenal dan menerapkan pestisida nabati berbahan daun mimba pada tanaman padi. Metode: Kegiatan dilaksanakan pada 29-30 Juli 2026 di RW 03, Kelurahan Margodadi, Kecamatan Metro Selatan, Kota Metro, Lampung, dengan melibatkan 23 anggota kelompok tani. Tahap kegiatan meliputi identifikasi permasalahan melalui observasi dan diskusi, penyampaian materi menggunakan powerpoint, diskusi dan tanya jawab, demonstrasi pembuatan ekstrak daun mimba oleh mahasiswa, serta pendampingan penerapan penggunaan pada tanaman. Evaluasi dilakukan secara deskriptif melalui observasi keterlibatan peserta, diskusi, tanya jawab, dan pengamatan dalam menerapkan teknik penyemprotan pestisida nabati terkait penurunan risiko ergonomi dan efektivitas pestisida yang digunakan. Hasil: Menunjukkan bahwa seluruh peserta (23 orang; 100%) mengikuti sesi edukasi dan pendampingan lapangan. Peserta terlibat aktif dalam diskusi, demonstrasi, serta penerapan teknik penggunaan tangki semprot dan pestisida nabati di lahan. Kegiatan memberikan pengenalan dan pengalaman praktis kepada mitra mengenai prinsip ergonomi dan pemanfaatan daun mimba sebagai alternatif pembasmi hama. Simpulan: Edukasi ergonomi dan pendampingan penerapan pestisida nabati daun mimba dapat dilaksanakan dengan baik dan efektif meningkatkan pemahaman masyarakat tentang pestisida terhadap kesehatan. Demonstrasi pembuatan pestisida nabati dengan pendampingan memberikan pengalaman langsung mengenai praktik ergonomi sederhana dalam penggunaan tangki semprot dan manfaat dari alternatif pestisida nabati. Saran: Kegiatan lanjutan disarankan menggunakan desain evaluasi yang lebih terukur, instrumen penilaian risiko ergonomi, dokumentasi keluhan muskuloskeletal, serta pengamatan kuantitatif populasi hama dan kerusakan tanaman.

items.title: Effect of AI authorship disclosure on purchase intention in cultural tourism souvenirs: The mediating roles of perceived effort and authenticity
items.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) expands in cultural tourism souvenir design and disclosure policies evolve, evidence remains limited on how AI authorship disclosure shapes responses across nationality groups and products. Drawing on signaling theory, two studies compared consumers from China and the U.S. across three disclosure conditions: unlabeled, human–AI co-created, and AI-generated. Study 1 used tourism postcard stimuli ( N = 1110), and Study 2 used mug and tourism tote bag stimuli ( N = 1255). Both studies found that disclosure affected purchase intention and interacted significantly with nationality. Differences across disclosure conditions were significant among participants from the U.S. but not among those from China. In Study 1, the unlabeled and human–AI co-created conditions did not differ, and both exceeded the AI-generated condition. In Study 2, the unlabeled condition exceeded both disclosed conditions for both products, whereas the latter two did not differ. AI-generated disclosure was consistently associated with lower purchase intention than no disclosure, whereas the relative position of human–AI co-created disclosure differed between studies. Parallel mediation analyses showed indirect effects through perceived effort and perceived authenticity. Perceived effort effects were significant for both comparisons with the unlabeled condition across three examined products, whereas the human–AI co-created versus unlabeled authenticity effect was nonsignificant in Study 1 but significant in Study 2. Nationality moderated some, but not all, indirect effects. Thus, firms should not assume that human–AI co-creation enhances responses and should consider clarifying human contribution and pretesting disclosure strategies across products and national markets.

items.title: Embodock: A robust embodied language-driven framework for vision-based AUV docking in turbid waters with zero-shot generalization
items.abstract: Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) docking in turbid, unstructured environments demands deliberative reasoning beyond reactive pixel-to-action mappings—existing geometry-based and end-to-end learning methods fail when visual features degrade or unforeseen scenarios occur. This paper proposes Embodock , an embodied language-driven framework that introduces Large Language Models (LLMs) as a cognitive core within a closed-loop Perceive-Reason-Act-Observe cycle. We formalize the docking task as a structured decomposition f = f act ∘ f reason ∘ f perceive and introduce three specific technical innovations: (i) a semantic persistence mechanism that maintains operational intent during visual dropout through structured token history; (ii) a vision-dominant multimodal prompt grammar that encodes temporal decision history and auxiliary telemetry alongside visual tokens, enabling context-aware compensation for external disturbances; and (iii) a three-tier Sim2Real pipeline combining knowledge distillation and LoRA fine-tuning to adapt foundation models to data-scarce subsea domains. items.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been significantly improved through deep learning techniques; however, the lack of interpretability remains a major challenge for clinical adoption. Methods: This study proposes an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-driven framework for multiclass brain tumor classification using a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) and four transfer learning models, namely ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0. The models were trained and evaluated on a publicly available brain MRI dataset consisting of glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumor classes. Their classification performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and confusion matrix analysis. To enhance transparency and interpretability, Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP were used to visualize and quantify the regions contributing to the classification decisions. Results: Experimental results state that the transfer learning models consistently outperformed the CNN by learning more discriminative feature representations while producing more localized and interpretable explanations. The agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP confirms that the proposed models predominantly relied on tumor regions rather than irrelevant background information, thereby improving the interpretability and reliability of the diagnostic predictions. Conclusions: The proposed framework provides an effective and explainable computer-aided diagnosis system that supports trustworthy deep learning-based brain tumor classification and has the potential for decision-making.

items.title: Empowerment of Islamic Religious Education Teachers through Generative AI Training for the Development of Islamic Value-Based Learning Media at SMP Negeri 35 Medan
items.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, particularly Generative AI, has created new opportunities for developing innovative, interactive, and contextual learning media. However, many Islamic Religious Education (IRE) teachers still have limited competencies in utilizing this technology as a learning medium while maintaining Islamic values. This Community Service Program (PKM) aimed to improve the competence of IRE teachers at SMP Negeri 35 Medan in utilizing Generative AI to develop creative, effective, and Islamic value-based learning media. The program employed a Participatory Action Learning approach consisting of needs identification, educational sessions, practical training, mentoring, and evaluation. The training involved demonstrations and hands-on practice using various Generative AI platforms, including ChatGPT, Canva AI, Gamma AI, and Microsoft Copilot, to develop teaching materials, presentations, assessment questions, and visual learning media based on Islamic values. The results indicated an improvement in participants' understanding of Generative AI, enhanced skills in developing digital learning media, and increased awareness of the ethical use of AI from an Islamic perspective. The teachers were able to produce learning media that were more engaging, interactive, contextual, and supportive of the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum. This program contributed positively to improving teachers' digital literacy while strengthening the integration of technology and Islamic values in the IRE learning process.

items.title: Engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing
items.abstract: Tools for manipulating RNA that rely on nonhuman proteins, such as ISC-based and Cas-based scaffolds, can lead to unintended and little-understood effects on human cells and present challenges in therapeutic translation. Replacing them with human proteins engineered for expanded, programmable functions could bypass the limitations of these foreign proteins. Here we demonstrate that human Argonaute 2 (AGO2) can be repurposed as a modular RNA targeting domain. AGO2 fused to a C-to-U deaminase enables AGO-led targeted editing of RNA (ALTER). Using guide RNAs that remodel target RNA structure for selective editing and reduced nuclease activity, we show that ALTER achieves, on average, 1.9-fold higher C-to-U editing on mRNA targets in HEK293T cells compared with Cas13 editors CURE and RESCUE. Transcriptome-wide RNA-seq revealed similar or lower levels of off-target editing compared to the same Cas13-based editors. Machine learning models predict that far fewer immunogenic peptides will result from ALTER and we show that ALTER is amenable to a validated workflow for artificial intelligence-directed deimmunization. Human Argonaute is repurposed for RNA editing.
